title: Involuntary downgrade with no delay and no cancellation
narrative: I paid for business class on a long flight and they put me in economy at the gate. The flight was on time. I assume I get the long-haul compensation amount.

documents.content:
BOOKING CE2081 — Passenger: B. NARDELLI (adult)
Carrier: Cerulean Eastern (CE)
CE118  FCO 19 Mar 2026 10:40  ->  SIN 20 Mar 2026 05:15
Cabin booked: BUSINESS. Fare paid for this segment: 800.00 units.
Great-circle distance FCO-SIN: 10,030 km.
Status: CONFIRMED.
BOARDING PASS CE118 19MAR2026 — NARDELLI/B — REISSUED AT GATE — seat 51H — cabin: ECONOMY (downgraded from 2A BUSINESS)

SIN ARRIVALS — CE118 20MAR2026
Scheduled on-blocks 05:15 local
Actual on-blocks 05:09 local
Delay at final destination: none, arrived 6 minutes early.

CERULEAN EASTERN OPS LOG — CE118 / 19MAR2026
Status: OPERATED ON TIME
Note: aircraft substitution, J-cabin 12 seats vs 30 booked. 18 passengers involuntarily downgraded to Y. Commercial decision, CE-controlled.

derivation: S2.1 no cancellation, no denied boarding, and the flight arrived early, so no Part 2 disruption qualifies
S7.2 a downgrade is not a Part 5 compensation event and Parts 4 and 5 do not apply to it
S7.1 reimbursement is 40% of the fare paid for the affected segment: 800.00 x 0.40 = 320 units
S6.1 duty of care is not engaged because no Part 2 disruption occurred
The claim is still worth submitting, for the S7.1 reimbursement only
